question: What was the traditional view of a man's primary role in family health?
explanation: Traditionally, men were viewed mainly as providers of money rather than active participants in daily health care and clinic visits. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: Why is involving men in family health beneficial for the household?

options.A: It improves health outcomes for women and children
options.B: It reduces the household income requirement
options.C: It makes clinic visits shorter for everyone
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses

explanation: Active male participation creates a supportive environment that directly boosts health and wellness for mothers and children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: Which socio-cultural factor most commonly discourages men from seeking early healthcare?

options.C: Fear of paying high transport costs
options.D: Viewing health-seeking behavior as a sign of weakness

explanation: Traditional definitions of masculinity often make men hide illness or delay seeking help to appear strong. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: What is the primary effect of patriarchal structures on family health responsibilities?

options.A: Men take on all nursing duties at home
options.B: Children become responsible for their own care
options.C: Health and domestic matters are left entirely to women
options.D: Couples share all medical decisions equally

explanation: Patriarchal norms often assign all caregiving and domestic duties to women, keeping men away from health spaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of a man attending antenatal care visits with his partner?

options.A: He replaces the midwife during delivery
options.B: He can perform the physical examination himself
options.C: He learns about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness
options.D: He receives free medications for chronic illnesses

explanation: Attending antenatal visits helps fathers understand what complications to watch out for and how to prepare for emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: A pregnant woman comes to the clinic with her husband who actively asks about emergency transport plans. How should the nurse view this behavior?

options.A: As a positive sign of male involvement in maternal health
options.B: As an unnecessary intrusion into clinical matters
options.C: As proof that the woman cannot care for herself
options.D: As a violation of hospital privacy policies

explanation: Planning for emergency transport with a partner shows strong male involvement which protects maternal and newborn health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: Why is male involvement important in family planning decisions?

options.A: It reduces the cost of buying medications
options.B: It gives men total control over family size
options.C: It removes the need for female contraceptive use
options.D: It ensures joint agreement and supports birth spacing

explanation: Family planning works best when both partners discuss and agree on methods that protect the health of the mother. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h4)

question: What is a common misconception regarding family planning services in many communities?

options.A: It is only meant for couples with no children
options.B: It is exclusively a female responsibility
options.C: It is completely free at all hospitals
options.D: It is dangerous for men to discuss it

explanation: Many people incorrectly believe that contraception and birth spacing concern only women, leaving men out of the conversation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier keeping men away from health clinics?

options.A: Staff attitudes that treat men as unwelcome intruders
options.B: Clinics operating convenient evening and weekend hours
options.C: Long waiting times that clash with work schedules
options.D: Facility environments focused solely on mothers and babies

explanation: Convenient operating hours would actually encourage attendance, whereas the other options represent real barriers men face. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: Why do daily wage earners find it difficult to attend primary healthcare clinics during the day?

options.A: Clinics refuse to treat people who work in the informal sector
options.B: Transportation is completely unavailable during daytime hours
options.C: Doctors only consult patients during the night
options.D: They lose a day of critical income while waiting at the hospital

explanation: Long daytime waiting hours present a direct financial penalty for men who depend on daily wages to survive. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: How do male champions help improve men's participation in family health?

options.A: By setting a positive example and discussing health openly among peers
options.B: By paying all the medical bills for families in the community
options.C: By taking over the duties of healthcare providers at the clinic
options.D: By forcing other men to visit hospitals through legal action

explanation: Respected peers break down cultural barriers by openly sharing their own positive experiences with clinic attendance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h6)

question: A primary health center wants to attract more working fathers to clinics. Which strategy is most effective?

options.A: Stopping all maternal health services to focus only on men
options.B: Introducing flexible clinic hours or dedicated men's health desks
options.C: Banning women from entering the clinic alone
options.D: Punishing men who refuse to attend antenatal visits

explanation: Creating welcoming spaces and flexible schedules accommodates men's work realities and encourages them to participate. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h6)

question: What is a key action Nigerian nurses can take to promote male involvement?

options.A: Send police officers to bring absent fathers to the hospital
options.B: Ignore fathers in the waiting room to focus only on mothers
options.C: Actively invite men into consultation rooms and address both parents
options.D: Charge men extra fees for entering maternal health clinics

explanation: Nurses promote involvement by making fathers feel welcome and included in health discussions right from the start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: Why must nurses work to eliminate personal bias regarding gender roles in the clinic?

options.A: Hospital management requires all nurses to pass a gender exam
options.B: Biases prevent nurses from dispensing medications properly
options.C: Ministry of health guidelines ban nurses from talking to men
options.D: Biased attitudes can make men feel unwelcome and drive them away from care

explanation: When nurses act judgmentally or ignore fathers, it reinforces the belief that health clinics are not meant for men. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)
